findings.title: Verification document describes RC5 rather than the current release
findings.evidence: VERIFICATION.md identifies fe09629 and says subsequent commits only change documentation/screenshots, then binds the APK hash, certificate and acceptance results to 1.2.0-rc.5 / 11. app/build.gradle.kts:15-16 now builds 1.2.0 / 12.
findings.impact: The documented exact-artifact signature and same-certificate update acceptance do not establish those properties for the current release. A release reviewer cannot use the RC5 hash as validation of the version-12 APK.
findings.recommendation: Retain RC5 as explicitly historical evidence and add current release metadata/hash/certificate and a same-certificate update receipt tied to the final version-12 artifact.

signing_certificate_evidence.detail: No signing key or actual APK certificate was read. The document supplies a certificate fingerprint for RC5, which is a claim, not independent verification of the current APK. Gradle only configures production signing when DOSOS73_KEYSTORE is supplied; CI has no such environment setup and uses an ephemeral test key for debug device tests. This does not prove that a real production certificate is absent outside these files.

observations: No debuggable=true or test fault provider is declared in the main manifest; debug tooling/test manifest dependencies use debugImplementation. Final merged release-manifest absence is not proven by this scoped static read.
Release minification and resource shrinking are enabled. applicationId remains com.os73.dosos73 and versionCode 12 exceeds the documented RC5 code 11.

CI runtime matrix installs repackaged debug builds, while VERIFICATION.md explicitly treats signed release acceptance as separate. No claim that the CI matrix itself verifies release signing was inferred.
actions: Static read only; no repository modifications, build, emulator, publication or key access.
